heading: November 17 Update: Keep Profit, Collections and Construction Funding Separate
markdown: **November 17 update.** NVIDIA's FY27Q2 free cash flow was USD 21.341 billion, but DSO rose from 45 to 60 days. The company attributed this to extended payment terms on large, multiquarter contracts with some investment-grade customers; that alone does not establish overdue receivables. CoreWeave's new Q3 results show operating cash of USD 5.638 billion and cash purchases/construction of USD 23.558 billion for the first nine months, a difference of negative USD 17.920 billion. Net financing cash of USD 21.346 billion over the same period had already provided a buffer, so this difference cannot be described as an unfilled funding shortfall, nor does that financing establish operating payback. These periods preceded Huang's departure and cannot be attributed to the leadership event. Supplier profits also do not establish customers' payback. The next checks are subsequent collections, receivables aging, actual drawdowns and construction payments. Sections 14.4–14.5 in Chapter 14 specify the complete definitions. [NVIDIA CFO commentary](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000073/q2fy27cfocommentary.htm), [CoreWeave Q3 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1769628/000176962826000465/crwv-20260930.htm)

heading: November 17 Update: Governance Changes First Put New Support to the Test
markdown: **November 17 update.** Huang's departure requires renewed scrutiny of approvals and risk-taking for new NVIDIA support, but does not automatically terminate existing corporate contracts. Equity already invested, initial capacity orders, contingent guarantees and third-party capital targets must still be recorded separately by status and term. Cloud services for the company's own R&D cannot be described as customer rescue funding, and intended subleasing of data centers does not mean the obligations have been transferred. Several direct customers may also serve the same ultimate demand; investment, shipments, offtake and guarantees cannot be counted as four independent sources of demand. I will examine final agreements, actual capital contributions, termination conditions and replacement customers. Sections 14.3–14.4 in Chapter 14 distinguish the contracts and payment sequence without adding headline amounts into a new financing total. [Leadership 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000082/nvda-20261111.htm), [Q2 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000075/nvda-20260726.htm)

heading: November 17 Update: Examine Geography and Ultimate End Use Separately
markdown: **November 17 update.** BIS announced the remote-compute rule on November 16, with formal publication scheduled for November 19; it is not yet effective as of this research date. Equipment destinations and ultimate cloud users raise separate licensing questions. One exception cannot be extrapolated into a comprehensive exemption from review, nor can the rule be summarized as a ban on all generative APIs, microdramas or coding applications. NVIDIA classifies geographic revenue by the headquarters of direct customers, which cannot directly measure risk associated with ultimate compute use. China's substitution opportunities still depend on software adaptation, energy use, delivery and customer budgets; new orders may not translate into an equivalent amount of profit. Section 14.7 in Chapter 14 connects customer eligibility, acceptance, drawdowns and payments, without attributing all policy effects to the departure. [Federal Register public inspection notice](https://www.federalregister.gov/public-inspection/2026-23529/addressing-remote-access-to-advanced-semiconductors), [geographic revenue disclosure](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000075/nvda-20260726.htm)

heading: November 17 Update: Key-Person Risk Does Not Erase Differences Among Companies
markdown: **November 17 update.** I view Huang's departure as a test of coordination across institutions and the assumption of capital risk, rather than treating one person's reputation as all the company's technological assets. CUDA, systems, the supply chain and customer deployments have organizational continuity; new products, permanent succession and financing partnerships still require testing. NVIDIA, model providers, diversified cloud providers, asset-heavy operators and application companies face different pressures. Legacy cash generation and distribution can provide buffers, while long-term commitments can consume them. A finance executive serving as interim CEO does not establish that R&D must shrink; stronger capital discipline may instead improve long-term returns. Sections 14.2 and 14.8 in Chapter 14 set out the different links and counterevidence. This update does not reconstruct price targets using a common valuation date or fixed risk rankings based on leadership news. [Transition announcement](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-ceo-transition), [Rubin platform description](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/inside-the-nvidia-rubin-platform-six-new-chips-one-ai-supercomputer/)

heading: November 17 Update: An Earlier Credit Shock Requires Evidence from Contract Performance
markdown: **November 17 update.** The main window remains H1 2027 through H1 2028. The earlier-credit-shock path receives higher monitoring priority, but a stock-price decline does not count as fulfillment of the forecast. I would need to see actual changes in credit facilities or drawdown terms, delays in acceptance and collections, and transmission across multiple entities before escalating my judgment. CoreWeave's liquidity includes available credit, and prepayment contracts becoming cancelable does not mean refunds have occurred. These conditions matter more than headline totals. Partner financial institutions continuing to discuss projects is counterevidence that must be retained. Sections 14.5 and 14.9 in Chapter 14 specify the order of checks. This update does not prematurely cite NVIDIA results due only on November 18 Beijing time, and my responsibility to record the window as unfulfilled on June 30, 2028 if it does not materialize remains unchanged. [CoreWeave Q3 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1769628/000176962826000465/crwv-20260930.htm), [NVIDIA disclosure timing](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-ceo-transition)

heading: November 17 Update: Amplification Through Delay and Deliberate Slowdowns Require Different Conditions
markdown: **November 17 update.** Continued financing supports the judgment that "delay amplifies risk" only when collections still lag and new net firm obligations keep growing. Slower financing may expose a shortfall earlier, or prevent uneconomic expansion. Section 14.6 in Chapter 14 uses a purely hypothetical monthly project to compare delayed acceptance, lower prices and utilization, negotiated deferral of payments, and paid-in replacement equity. Negative cash means funding must first be filled for the path to be executed. Financing arriving improves liquidity without establishing better operating recovery from the assets. A deliberate slowdown requires counterparties' agreement and checks of penalties; it cannot assume all payments naturally move back. Depreciation affects the corresponding allocation of expenses to profit, and is not deducted again when the cash table already includes equipment payments. The example is not extrapolated into an industry funding shortfall or burst date; actual commitments remain governed by contracts. [NVIDIA Q2 contractual disclosures](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000075/nvda-20260726.htm)
